'''Mogens Høgh Jensen''' (born 2 March 1955) is a Danish physicist who has made contributions to the fields of complex dynamics and fractals. He currently holds a professorship at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]], [[University of Copenhagen]] and is the former president and secretary general of the [[Royal Danish Academy of Science and Letters]].

He received his master's degree in 1981, with professor [[Per Bak]] as supervisor. His master project was about “Theory of Helical Magnetic Structure and Phase Transitions” which was later devoted a chapter in [[L. D. Landau]] and [[E. M. Lifshitz]], ”Electrodynamics of Continuous Media” (Chap. 52).

During his PhD he worked on studies of [[chaos theory|chaos]] and [[fractal dimensions]] and with [[Per Bak]] and Tomas Bohr he discovered universal scaling structure of mode locking between two frequencies at the onset of chaos.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jensen |first1=Mogens Høgh |last2=Bak |first2=Per |last3=Bohr |first3=Thomas |title=Transition to chaos by interaction of resonances in dissipative systems. I. Circle maps |journal=Physical Review A|volume=30 |issue=4 |pages=1960 |bibcode=1984PhRvA..30.1960J |year=1984 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.30.1960 }}</ref>

Following his PhD in 1984, he continued his academic career as a postdoc at the [[James Franck Institute]] in Chicago, with [[Leo Kadanoff]] as his supervisor. Here he contributed to a series of highly influential papers, and most notably he played a key part in the development of multi fractals.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Halsey |first1=Thomas C |last2=Jensen |first2=Mogens Høgh |last3=Kadanoff |first3=Leo P. |last4=Procaccia |first4=Itamar |last5=Shraiman |first5=Boris |title=Fractal measures and their singularities: The characterization of strange sets |journal=Physical Review A}}</ref>

He later worked on fully developed turbulence and together with Giovanni Paladin and Angelo Vulpiani he pioneered the study of intermittency correction in term of shell models.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bohr |first1=Tomas |last2=Jensen |first2=Mogens Høgh |last3=Paladin |first3=Giovanni |last4=Vulpiani |first4=Angelo |title=Dynamical systems approach to turbulence |publisher=Cambridge University Press}}</ref> He was the head of ‘Center for Chaos and Turbulence Studies: CATS’ before he in 2004 he became the director of ‘BioNET: Danish Center for Biophysics’. Since then he has mainly worked on problems in [[biological physics]], in particular protein [[oscillations]] inside cells.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Heltberg |first1=Mathias L |last2=Kellogg |first2=Ryan |last3=Krishna |first3=Sandeep |last4=Tay |first4=Savas |last5=Jensen |first5=Mogens Høgh |title=Noise induces hopping between NF-κB entrainment modes |journal=Cell Systems}}</ref>

He has received several prizes most notably the Norwegian physics prize ‘Gunnar Randers’ handed over in 2011 by King [[Harald V of Norway]].

He has been visiting professor at the Universities in Chicago, Rome, Fukuoka and [[Harvard]].

Mogens Høgh Jensen has been at a member of the Royal Danish Academy of Science and Letters since 2000, its secretary general in the period 2012–2016 and the president since 2016. He was knighted by [[Queen Margrethe II]] in 2017.
